expectation: Membrane ring on B cells. In tumour tissue they are few, scattered single cells, packed into dense lymphoid aggregates or tertiary lymphoid structures. Most fields should be negative, with some focal compact clusters of bright cells.
observed: A: compact bright clusters in a few ROIs, one of them a large dense aggregate, plus sparse scattered cells; most ROIs are negative. B and C are almost empty, with one small cell in C. D shows packed cells with clear membrane rings around dark nuclei.
why: CD20 picks out dense, focal aggregates that look like lymphoid structures, made of cells with membrane rings, while the surrounding tissue is negative. That is the pattern expected of B cells.
notes: CD20 lights up a few compact aggregates (one large) that look like lymphoid follicles. Up close, the cells there have clear membrane rings. Other fields have only sparse cells, so the empty B and C fields fit a focal population rather than a failed stain.
